subject: Action required: credit plan for token duplication incident (BrightLeaf)
messages:
From: Sienna Carter <sienna@brightleaf.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: BrightLeaf Billing <billing@brightleaf.ai>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected duplicate charges on Sep 23 invoice

Hi Kimberly,

We noticed something concerning on our September 23 invoice (Invoice ID: BL-2026-09-23-117). Several line items show token counts that appear to be duplicated — e.g., the /generate endpoint shows ~1.2M tokens on top of expected volumes for the day.

Can you confirm whether this is correct? This spike caused us to exceed our committed spend for the month and triggered an internal alert. Attached is the invoice snippet we exported from our billing system.

We need a timeline for investigation and a plan for corrective credits. Our procurement team is waiting for a formal response so we can reconcile on our side.

Thanks,
Sienna
Head of DevOps
BrightLeaf AI

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Unexpected duplicate charges on Sep 23 invoice

Hi Sienna — thank you for flagging this and sharing the snippet. I'm really sorry for the disruption.

I've opened an internal investigation and looped in finance and engineering. We'll prioritize this and share an initial status update within 24 hours and a remediation plan within 72 hours.

For visibility, the team on copy is: Marissa (Billing), Rishi (Infra/Runtime), Marcus (SRE). Sean (Account Exec) is on the thread and will be available for procurement conversations.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com, marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: BrightLeaf invoice — triage and proposed actions

Team — following up on BrightLeaf's report. Initial ask: confirm whether they were double-billed (token-count duplication) on 2026-09-23 and produce proposed credit amount + timeline for applying the adjustment.

What I have so far:
- Customer observed a large token spike on Sep 23 tied to the /generate endpoint (they provided invoice snippet).
- Customer is paused on reconciliations until we confirm credits.

Please investigate and provide:
1) Root cause hypothesis and confirmation window (UTC).
2) Exact duplicated token count (per invoice line) and the dollar credit to be applied.
3) Recommended customer-facing wording and timeline for when the credit will appear on their ledger.

Rishi — can you pull the request logs and any retry-id headers for the 23rd (00:00–12:00 UTC) and verify if any replays or double-execs occurred? Marcus — confirm whether billing aggregation logic would have double-counted if a request was reprocessed. Marissa — provisional estimate of credit mechanics (invoice adjustment vs. immediate account credit).

Thanks,
Kimberly
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com, marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com
Cc: sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com
Date: Mon, 27 Sep 2026 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: BrightLeaf invoice — triage and proposed actions

Team — investigation findings (summary):

Root cause: transient bug in the idempotency/ingestion layer during a short rollout on 2026-09-23 (approx 04:00–07:30 UTC). When a small percentage of requests arrived with a missing/expired idempotency header, our retry handler retried at the gateway layer and re-enqueued the request without deduping, which led to double-processing for those requests. The runtime recorded two token usage entries for the same logical request.

Scope: affected customer sessions where the client retried at the app layer during the rollout window — estimated duplication applies to a subset of calls to /generate (we found repeated request-ids with same prompt hashes).

Counts and proposed credit:
- Duplicated tokens (BrightLeaf, aggregated): 1,237,890 tokens.
- Pricing basis used: $0.004435 per 1k tokens (their tier).
- Calculated credit: $5,481.23 (rounded to two decimals).

Attachments: small sample CSV of matched double entries for Sep 23 (usage_log_snippet.csv) — includes request_id, prompt_hash, first_ts, second_ts, tokens_first, tokens_second.

Recommendation: issue a direct invoice adjustment for the duplicated tokens and reflect as a negative line on their October invoice, with a ledger reference. Also propose issuing a one-time 10% goodwill credit on the duplicated amount ($548.12) given the operational impact. Total adjustment: $6,029.35.

I'll coordinate with billing to produce the ledger entry once Marissa confirms the mechanism. Marcus — we've pushed a hotfix to the retry logic and added a monitoring alert to detect any future missing-idempotency duplicate patterns.

— Rishi
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sienna Carter <sienna@brightleaf.ai>
Cc: BrightLeaf Billing <billing@brightleaf.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com, marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com
Date: Tue, 28 Sep 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Resolution and credit plan for Sep 23 token duplication (BrightLeaf)

Hi Sienna —

Thank you again for raising this. We've completed a technical investigation and confirmed that a small fraction of BrightLeaf requests were double-processed during a rollout window on Sep 23 (approx 04:00–07:30 UTC). The root cause was a retry/idempotency gap at our gateway that has been fixed; monitoring is in place.

What we'll do next (agreement requested):
- Credit: We will apply an invoice adjustment for the duplicated tokens. Identified duplicated tokens: 1,237,890 → credit amount $5,481.23.
- Goodwill: Redwood will also apply a one-time 10% goodwill credit on the duplicated amount ($548.12).
- Total adjustment: $6,029.35.
- Timing: The negative line will be included on your October invoice and should post to your account ledger within 5 business days of your acknowledgement. If you prefer an immediate account-level credit instead of an October invoice line, we can do that — let us know.

Attached is a short adjustment summary and the usage sample we relied on.

Next steps we propose:
1) You confirm acceptance of the adjustment and whether you prefer invoice-line credit or immediate account credit.
2) We will generate a ledger reference and send a short confirmation email once applied.

We apologize for any disruption this caused. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk through the findings and the logs.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Resolution and credit plan for Sep 23 token duplication (BrightLeaf)

Kimberly — thanks for the thorough investigation and the proposed remediation. BrightLeaf accepts the total adjustment of $6,029.35 and we'd prefer an immediate account credit so the refund shows up ahead of our monthly reconciliation.

Please send the ledger reference once posted. I attached our internal PO for the credit application (PO_BrightLeaf_0928.pdf). We also appreciate the goodwill gesture — that helps smooth this on our end.

Thanks,
Sienna
